endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Preconditions include that a patient must have a diagnosis of asthma in the EHR, patient data must be available in the EHR, and pediatric clinician chart review and treatment decision making can be done leveraging the summary of clinical information, AE risk score, and list of actionable intervention options.

evidence.title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
evidence.outcome: Coding F-score with more complete clinical-section inputs
evidence.effect: Full-section inclusion increased F-score from 0.786 after deduplication to 0.798. External full-code F-scores increased from 0.764 to 0.779 at KMUH RCT and from 0.626 to 0.636 at TMMH.
evidence.quote: Finally, comparing these results from redundancy-aware sampling revealed complementary effects on downstream performance: the F-score increased from 0.780 (baseline) to 0.786 ( + deduplication) and 0.798 ( + full section inclusion).
evidence.sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

evidence.title: Evaluating the Utility of Personal Health Records in Personalized Health AI
evidence.outcome: Answer helpfulness with vs without PHR context provided to the LLM
evidence.effect: Significant improvements in helpfulness for all question types with PHR data (p < 0.001, paired t-test); potential gains in safety, accuracy, relevance and personalization.
evidence.quote: We see significant improvements in the helpfulness of answers to all question types with PHR data (p < 0.001, paired t-test).

evidence.title: Ambient Only vs. Longitudinal Data-Enhanced AI Documentation: A Pilot Study Quantifying the Value of Historical Clinical Context in Primary Care
evidence.outcome: QNOTE assessment composite score for ambient-only vs ambient plus historical EHR data
evidence.effect: Consolidated documentation scored higher than ambient-only (94.8 vs. 80.1; difference 14.6 points; 95% CI 13.4-15.8; P<0.001); completeness difference 42.5 points.
evidence.quote: Consolidated documentation achieved significantly higher mean total assessment composite score compared to ambient-only (94.8 vs. 80.1 on a scale of 0-100; difference 14.6 points; 95% CI 13.4-15.8; P<0.001).

evidence.title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
evidence.effect: Accuracy increased from 12% to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentation were added; P<0.001.
evidence.quote: With the "only visual" input format, browser-based GPT-5 achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 12%, increasing to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentations were provided (P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Generating subjective, objective, assessment, and plan (SOAP)-structured medication logs using DeepSeek-R1 through prompt engineering and multi-source clinical information
evidence.quote: All three raters agreed that text generated from multi-information-source was superior to text from single-information-source with consistently higher mean 7DI scores across prompts (e.g. Prompt 4—Rater 1: 29.35 ± 1.54 vs. 25.66 ± 1.90; Rater 2: 29.55 ± 2.92 vs. 25.15 ± 1.77; Rater 3: 30.60 ± 1.85 vs. 27.49 ± 2.07; all P < 0.01; Supplemental Table 3 ).

evidence.title: Exploring GPT-4o's multimodal reasoning capabilities with panoramic radiograph: the role of prompt engineering
evidence.effect: Recall increased from 2.67 to 43.33% when PRs were provided (P < 0.001).
evidence.quote: In the ablation study, GPT-4o's recall increased significantly from 2.67 to 43.33% upon acquiring PRs (P < 0.001).

evidence.title: DEPLOYR: a technical framework for deploying custom real-time machine learning models into the electronic medical record
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Model performance stratified by available feature count
evidence.effect: Performance increased with the number of available features at inference time; numerical effect estimates were not provided in the text.
evidence.quote: We show that performance of our ML models increases with the number of available features at inference time.
evidence.sample_unit: machine learning models (laboratory result classifiers) silently deployed

evidence.title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
evidence.outcome: Missing patient data and predictive accuracy
evidence.effect: Withheld clinical data lowered AUROC/AUPRC; reintroducing data increased AUROC 0.896 to 0.918 and AUPRC 0.336 to 0.352.
evidence.quote: The AUROC increased from 0.896 to 0.918 (95% CI: 0.912–0.924; DeLong test p < 0.001), and the AUPRC increased from 0.336 (95% CI: 0.312–0.361) to 0.352 (95% CI: 0.329–0.373), further enhancing the model’s predictive capabilities.

evidence.title: Medical Knowledge Is Not All You Need: When Medical Q&A Becomes Situated Patient Assistance
evidence.effect: 41.9% of response-requiring questions depended on information beyond the procedure: visual/physical state, environmental context, or prior actions.
evidence.quote: In a study with 73 skin cancer patients practicing postoperative wound care, 41.9% of response-requiring questions depended on information beyond the procedure, including visual or physical state, environmental context, or prior actions.

evidence.title: Addressing the implementation challenge of risk prediction model due to missing risk factors: The submodel approximation approach
evidence.outcome: inability to calculate risk prediction due to missing risk factors
evidence.effect: more than 30% of acute heart failure patients had at least one missing risk factor, preventing risk calculation in its original form
evidence.quote: Preliminary EHR data extraction of STRATIFY risk factors revealed more than 30% of AHF patients had at least one missing STRATIFY risk factor at the time of disposition decision making, and thus cannot have STRATIFY risk calculated in its original form.

evidence.title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: errors from missing or ambiguous data
evidence.effect: Complex inclusion/exclusion caused 54.5% of errors; ambiguous contexts including missing information caused 39.3%.
evidence.quote: Adjudication revealed that while the model excelled at identifying when there was a deprescribing criterion related to one of the patient's medications, it often struggled with determining whether that criterion applied to the specific case due to complex inclusion and exclusion criteria (54.5% of errors) and ambiguous clinical contexts (eg, missing information; 39.3% of errors).

evidence.title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
evidence.outcome: Recommendations reflecting available prior patient data (longitudinal recall)
evidence.effect: AI recommended genetic testing for a patient who had already undergone testing, reflecting limitation in longitudinal data recall.
evidence.quote: In another case, the AI recommended GT for a patient who had already undergone testing.

evidence.title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
evidence.effect: 4009 ALI components were missing; 789 (20%) were recovered by the algorithm.
evidence.quote: Of 4009 missing ALI components, 789 ( 20 % ) were recovered.

evidence.title: Concordance between GPT-4 and a multidisciplinary tumor board in pancreatic cancer: A prospective pilot study
evidence.effect: Incomplete data in the MDT referral explained three of 12 non-concordant cases (25.0%).
evidence.quote: Among the 12 non-concordant cases, the presumed cause of discordance was an inadequate capture of clinical complexity by GPT-4 in three cases (25.0%), incomplete data in the MDT referral in three cases (25.0%) and a disregard of essential clinical data by GPT-4 in one case (8.3%).

evidence.title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation vs. Long-Context Input for Clinical Reasoning over EHRs
evidence.outcome: Effect of missing patient data (inter-hospital transfers) on LLM EHR task performance
evidence.effect: Error analysis showed missing information in clinical notes, often due to inter-hospital transfers, limited performance to some extent.
evidence.quote: Error analysis revealed that missing information in the clinical notes--often due to inter-hospital transfers--limited performance to some extent.

evidence.title: IMCBench: A benchmark for multimodal LLMs in Image-grounded Medical Conversations
evidence.outcome: Change in safety score when EHR context or visual input removed
evidence.effect: Safety dropped by 0.23 on average when EHR context was removed and by 0.18 when visual input was removed; stronger models used visual features more effectively.
evidence.quote: Ablation studies further reveal that both visual input and EHR context contribute to safe guidance (safety drops of 0.18 and 0.23 on average when each is removed), with stronger models leveraging visual features more effectively.

evidence.title: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation versus long-context input for clinical reasoning over electronic health records
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Effect of missing patient data in notes on task performance
evidence.effect: Error analysis found missing information in the clinical notes, often due to inter-hospital transfers, limited performance to some extent.
evidence.quote: Error analysis revealed that missing information in the clinical notes-often due to inter-hospital transfers-limited performance to some extent.

evidence.title: An agentic AI framework connecting language models to electronic health records and a biomedical knowledge graph for real-world evidence
evidence.effect: OMOP standardization may incompletely capture specialty panels or local codes, reducing event counts and statistical power.
evidence.quote: This attenuation likely reflects differences in data architecture between the Clinical Data Warehouse used in the original study—which provided direct access to all laboratory values—and the OMOP data model used in our replication, where laboratory results undergo vocabulary standardization that may incompletely capture specialty panels or non-standard local codes, reducing both event counts and statistical power.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark clinical research questions (400 model-configuration runs); plus 617 BiomixQA questions

commentary.bottom_line: Six studies found that giving AI tools more complete patient data improved output quality, including one randomized trial in which fuller discharge-summary inputs raised coding F-scores from 0.786 to 0.798. No study tested cross-system retrieval as a deployment safeguard or measured patient outcomes, so the evidence supports the direction of the practice more than its specific form.

perspectives.view: One randomized trial in real deployment showed F-score gains of about 0.01 to 0.015 with full-section inputs. The other five studies are offline replays or benchmarks that rely on rater scores, accuracy, or recall. All six point in the same direction, but indirectness and surrogate outcomes lower certainty to low.

In a live deployment, withheld data lowered AUROC, and restoring the data raised it from 0.896 to 0.918. One tool recommended genetic testing a patient had already completed. In a benchmark, recall of inserted interpretation errors rose from 2.67% to 43.33% when the panoramic radiographs were provided. None of these studies measured harm that reached patients.

Adding historical EHR data to ambient notes raised composite quality from 80.1 to 94.8. Multi-source inputs also improved pharmacist-rated medication logs. Two benchmarks traced missing note content to inter-hospital transfers, which suggests retrieval across systems may matter. No study measured retrieval burden, latency, or fidelity within clinical workflow.

The only test with a flagged population was a non-English offline replay of 80 medication logs from China. No test included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy patients. Patients whose care is split across unaffiliated systems may have more fragmented records, and no study examined whether retrieval closes that gap for them.

Adding personal health record context improved the rated helpfulness of answers to 2,257 queries (p < 0.001). This suggests patients may receive more relevant answers when their own data are used. No study asked patients about consent to cross-system retrieval, or whether fuller data changed their trust or their access to a clinician.

commentary.research_gap: No study compared deployments with and without cross-system retrieval. None measured how often retrieval fills missing fields in routine practice, and none tracked clinical errors or patient outcomes. A pragmatic trial at sites with high inter-hospital transfer rates would test the practice directly if it reported retrieval completeness, staff workload, and downstream errors.
commentary.underserved_note: One test, the pharmacist-rated medication-log study, took place in a non-English setting in China. No test included Medicaid or safety-net patients, patients with limited English proficiency in English-dominant health systems, or low-literacy populations. Systems serving these groups have no direct evidence that the reported gains apply to their records or patients.
